{"content": "# SSD Definition

SSD stands for **Solid-State Drive** (or Solid State Drive). 

## Overview
An SSD is a type of non-volatile computer storage device that uses integrated circuit assemblies (typically flash memory) to store data persistently. Unlike traditional hard disk drives (HDDs), SSDs contain no moving mechanical parts, resulting in faster read/write speeds, lower power consumption, and greater physical reliability.
